sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 2001. The Proto Trans New Guinea obstruents: arguments from top-down reconstruction. In Andrew Pawley, Malcolm Ross & Darrell Tryon (eds.), The boy from Bundaberg: Studies in Melanesian linguistics in honour of Tom Dutton, 261-300. Pacific Linguistics 514. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/254062, file, 40 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing on Lemio prosody. The only suprasegmental remark is family-wide and explicitly sets prosody aside: 'A number of TNG languages are tonal, with considerable typological variety in the systems (Donohue 1997), but only segmental phonemes will be considered here.' (printed p. 271 = p. 11). Table 2 'Segmental phonemes in some contemporary TNG languages' does not include Lemio or any Kabenau language. Lemio appears only as lexical reflexes in cognate sets (e.g. Lemio bapa, simp, ger, indi-, rha-, du:k, [a]lokam 'eye', khon, kumo- 'die', ngari-), unmarked for stress -- wordlist-level data onl…

sources.citation: Roberts, John R. 1997. Switch-reference in Papua New Guinea: a preliminary survey. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan Linguistics No. 3, 101-241. Pacific Linguistics A-87. Canberra: ANU. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253643)
sources.note: No phonology content (morphosyntactic survey). Useful negative evidence on data availability: p. 115, sec. 2.2.33: 'In the Kabenau family SS/DS is reported to occur in the Siroi language. For the Arawum, Kolom, Lemio, and Pulabu languages there is no information available [as] to whether they have SS/DS or not.' Appendix table (p. 108): 'Arawum, Kolom, Lemio, Pulabu: no information available'.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-D30 (sealang.net open CC BY-SA scan)
sources.note: Nothing. Lemio = language B9 in a c. 300-item comparative wordlist. Intro sec. 7 (p. vii): 'The transcription of the word list is rendered in a semiphonemic form'; fluctuating sounds listed for Lemio f~p, g~fricative (p. viii). No mention of stress, accent or tone anywhere in the introduction (pp. v-x); Lemio forms carry aspiration and vowel length but no stress marks (visual check, printed p. 3 =).

sources.note: Nothing; classificatory only (Kabenau family = Arawum, Kolom, Suroi, Lemio, Pulabu; Claassen & McElhanon's Gurumbu and Lemio are one language).
